instagram_recent_posts.excerpt: Few people know I almost quit @google three months in because the pressure was intense and I didn’t feel like I belonged. I ended up staying by reminding myself what I worked so hard to achieve: free food 🙃 . 8 years passed in a blink of an eye. Thanks for being the best thing that’s happened to me 😁

Flew to #googleio and took more notes in two days than I did in 9 years as an employee 🤓. Jokes aside, what an absolutely incredible week. Top 3 personal highlights: 1️⃣ Interviewed Josh Woodward (Head of Google Gemini) 2️⃣ Met some of the most talented and friendly creators from all over the world 3️⃣ Got to meet and chat with SO MANY of you in person!!!! Looking back on the past few years, one saying keeps coming to mind: 🙏 What a privilege it is to be tired from the work I once begged the universe for. 🙏 What a privilege to feel overwhelmed by the growth I once dreamed about. 🙏 What a privilege to be challenged by a life I created on purpose. Thanks @google and see you next year (hopefully)! 😁
🇮🇹 Pro tip on how to piss off every Italian person you meet: “Yea can I get some ketchup with that?”

I taught the Master Prompt: one document that tells any AI who you are, what you're working on, and how you make decisions, so you stop re-explaining yourself from scratch in every new chat. Missed it? Full recording's up: Link in bio! Enrollment for Cohort 2 is open, and the 25% off early bird pricing ends today at 2 PM ET. If you've been on the fence, this is the window. Join via the link in my bio!

Most AI failures right now have nothing to do with the technology. They're context failures. The AI doesn't know enough about you, your work, or how you think. The instinct is to fix that by feeding it everything: every file, every doc, every note you've got. But context isn't free. Recent research shows LLMs start to break down once their context window is only 30 to 40% full. Overload them, and they forget details, miss connections, and get confused by conflicting information. It's called context rot, and it's getting worse, not better. So the skill that matters now is curation: the right pieces, broken into modules, loaded only when you need them. And that takes a different identity: from a doer at the front lines to the architect of a system, deciding what information matters, when to bring it in, and how to structure it so AI can use it. I'm teaching how to build that system in Cohort 2 of The AI Second Brain. Enrollment is open now through Sep. 15. Link in bio!
